title: FieldPoly batch evaluation via subproduct tree
description:
Add `batch_evaluate(&self, points: &[F]) -> Vec<F>` to `FieldPoly<F>` using the subproduct-tree algorithm (O(n log² n) *with fast polynomial division*).

## Algorithm

1. Leaves `M_i = x - point_i` (length 2).
2. Internal nodes: products of children (reuse `FieldPoly::mul` Karatsuba-enabled path).
3. Top-down reduction: reduce `self` modulo each internal subproduct (reuse `div_rem`).
4. Leaf values are the evaluations.

## API

- `pub fn batch_evaluate(&self, points: &[F]) -> Vec<F>`.
- Fallback to per-point Horner when `points.len() < SUBPRODUCT_THRESHOLD` or `self.degree() < SUBPRODUCT_THRESHOLD`; threshold as a named `const` tuned by the benchmark in `benches/field_poly.rs`.

## Success criteria

- Agreement proptest: `batch_evaluate(points) == points.iter().map(|p| evaluate(p)).collect()` over both `Fp<7>` and `Gf2mElement`.
- Unit tests: `k=1`, `k=2`, duplicate points, points containing zero, degree-0 polynomial, zero polynomial input.
- Subproduct-tree infrastructure in place (tree construction, root-down reduction) correctly implements the standard algorithm; the tree layout is documented; the threshold constant is tuned from benchmark data.
- New Criterion bench at `crates/gf2-core/benches/field_poly.rs` measures `batch_evaluate_subproduct` (the raw tree path, exposed for benchmarking) vs `k` individual Horner evaluations on `Fp<65537>` across `n, k ∈ {16, 64, 256, 1024}`. The measured table is committed into the module docstring (mirror `batch_ops.rs`).
- **Asymptotic win deferred to `e0b6f940` (NTT-based polynomial multiplication + fast division, Task 7).** With the current schoolbook `FieldPoly::div_rem` the tree's per-node reduction cost `O(n · k)` dominates the product-tree's `O(n log k)` build cost, so on cheap scalar fields (`Fp<65537>` mul ≈ 3.6 ns) the public `batch_evaluate` routes through the naive Horner fallback at practical sizes. Once `e0b6f940` adds fast `mod` via FFT-Newton, the threshold can drop and the tree path takes over — this issue ships the infrastructure that Task 7 will then flip on.
- `cargo fmt` / `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` / `cargo test --release` clean; budget ≤ 60 s.

## Scope revision (2026-04-19)

Original criterion read: *"Criterion bench shows subproduct-tree beats k individual Horner evaluations for `k >= 16, n >= 16` on `Fp<65537>`."* The executing agent measured every cell in the `n × k ∈ {16, 64, 256, 1024}` matrix and reported that naive Horner wins everywhere on schoolbook `div_rem` — the tree's asymptotic `O(n log² n)` advantage only materialises with NTT-backed fast polynomial division, which is tracked by Task 7 (`e0b6f940`). The criterion has been softened to: infrastructure + tuned threshold + documented benchmark table, with the actual performance crossover promised on `e0b6f940`'s closure.
